resolved: Ofannim (khevodo_ahel), HE and EN: six stanza milestones. Stanza 5 opens unconditionally at the start of its tei:p, before the weekday (shabbat=false) and Shabbat (shabbat=true, type="marked") branches. The final bare stanza terminator is present.
HE khevodo_ahel standOff note for /5 ('וי״א …') now has j:condition as its first child (shabbat=true).
Both languages mark the Shabbat variant with type="marked". The made-up weekday rubric and the made-up EN Shabbat rubric are gone. The printed HE 'אם שבת' stays on the Shabbat branch.

HE Rashi role notes (ח׳ = reader, קו״ח = reader_and_congregation) are encoded where they occur in stanzas 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Their letter readings are still pending adjudication and I haven't certified them.

Kaddish intro: the English 'The Reader says half Kaddish.' printed on HE n95 is now before the Numbers 14:17 verse, with role/reader corresp. EN has its own printed intro in the same place. The HE חזן label stays at the start of the Kaddish yitgaddal prayer-part.
Hakol (HE n101 / EN n102) has its own pb n=37 and its own printed Shabbat rubric as the conditional's first-child note.

El Adon, HE and EN: the repeated Shabbat heading at the page 38 continuation is a nested conditional rubric inside the outer shabbat=true conditional. So the rubric is redundant, and hidden, when Shabbat is known to be true.
The documentary routing rubrics are in the index right before Hameir: HE yi note at n101, EN note at n102. They are not in the transcluded module, and I'm not counting them as missing.
Prior issue 1 accepted: Ps 104:24 in Hameir is the first canonical mapping, so the bible URN corresp is allowed.

Prior issue 2 accepted: chapter milestone with @n, then verse, then bare verse and chapter terminators, follows the established pattern. In lael_asher_shavat, 92:1 and 92:2 share a boundary with a redundant terminator and reopen, which loses no text.

Prior issue 3 accepted: the partial Isaiah 6:3, Ezekiel 3:12 and Ps 92:1/92:2 use only occurrence-context URNs, with seg type="quotation" and a canonical source. No new full-verse Bible corresp is claimed. Consistent in both languages.
Prior issue 4 accepted: Az Yashir range syntax is out of scope and unchanged.
observations: The HE and EN module sets match one-to-one across all 20 stems. In each pair, conditional IDs, conditions, stanza/prayer-part/verse milestones and quorum conditionals are the same. Page facs alternate correctly (HE odd n95–n107, EN even n96–n108), and printed page numbers agree.

The EN El Adon nested rubric opens mid-clause ('merit and equity are | On Sabbath. | before His throne'), at the EN page break. The HE one opens at a line boundary. Both are faithful to where the page breaks fall. Because the outer condition is the same, this only affects display when Shabbat is unknown.
EN khevodo_ahel has no counterpart to the HE standOff note 'וי״א …' and no role notes. That's fine if the EN page prints neither. Worth checking in the human pass.
Titbarakh ends mid-sentence ('…crown' / 'וּמַמְלִיכִים') and continues into et_shem in both languages, so the split is aligned.

Source wording I noticed but haven't judged (left for humans 1–5): EN Barekhu 'Blessed be Him, His Name is exalted above and ever.'; HE khevodo_ahel stanza 1 opening; the ייָ vs יְיָ divine-name forms after a prefix in Hakol and La'el Asher Shavat. The EN sic/corr pairs in lael_asher_shavat and melekh_azur_gevurah are well formed.
This is structural draft review only, not source acceptance.
